text:
oncall-bot: :warning: Incident 2026-03-15-ORBIT-GW-RETRYSTORM: high reconnects and 429/502 errors observed for tenant orbitfin in us-east-2. Paging on-call.
Mira: I'm oncall. seeing surge in 429s and websocket reconnects for orbitfin. Dashboard shows retry spikes starting ~16:05 UTC.
Elena (OrbitFin): confirmed from our side: customers see data latency spikes and dashboard reconnect banners since ~11:05 ET. No config changes from OrbitFin.
Raj: pulling gateway logs. Pattern: our per-tenant token rate limiter started returning 429 + `Retry-After: 0` to existing client library; clients interpret that as immediate retry loop. Getting a retry storm that exhausts worker threads.
Priya: interesting. Any deploys recently to rate-limiter or auth service?
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: auth-service@v3.4.7 deployed to us-east-2 at 2026-03-15T15:58:12Z. No rollbacks.
Raj: that matches. I see changed header handling in v3.4.7 where `Retry-After` was accidentally set to 0 for some token error cases.
Mira: that would cause immediate reconnects in many client SDKs. Elena, which SDK versions are your clients on?
Elena (OrbitFin): majority are on OrbitFin webapp using our SDK v1.8.2 which honors Retry-After header; some older mobile clients do immediate exponential retries without observing server Retry-After.
Ken: impact summary: ~60% of websocket connect attempts for orbitfin failing within 2s and then flooding the gateway, causing a cascade -> some upgrade requests get 502 due to worker exhaustion. Severity: P1 (tenant-scoped).
Mira: mitigation plan options: 1) patch auth-service to return sensible Retry-After (e.g., 15s) and roll immediately; 2) add a temporary tenant-scoped rate-limit bypass + circuit-breaker for orbitfin to break the retry loop; 3) route orbitfin traffic to dedicated-us-east-03 where we can raise concurrency limits; 4) push server-side outbound 429 throttling with `Retry-After` header and set `Connection: close` to force exponential backoff at client.
Raj: patching auth-service is fastest long-term fix. For immediate relief, we should (A) deploy tenant route to dedicated-us-east-03 and (B) apply per-tenant circuit-breaker to drop aggressive reconnects for 30s windows.
Priya: dedicated-us-east-03 utilization at 48%, can accept the tenant. Note: token pinning exists; ensure we preserve session affinity when moving. Use `rbctl route set --tenant orbitfin --target dedicated-us-east-03 --preserve-affinity=true`.
Mira: executing dry-run then apply.
Mira: `rbctl route set --tenant orbitfin --target dedicated-us-east-03 --preserve-affinity=true --dry-run` -> ok. Applying now. Route applied at 16:14:37 UTC.
oncall-bot: Audit: route change detected for tenant orbitfin at 1965432160.
Ken: applying transient circuit-breaker: set `tenant_rate_limit[orbitfin].burst=50` and `window=30s` with drop policy for excessive reconnects. Pushed at 16:15:22 UTC.
Raj: starting emergency patch to auth-service to ensure `Retry-After` >= 10s for token throttle paths. Pushing build and will hotfix.
Priya: monitoring after route and CB; initial reconnect rate dropped from 62% -> 9% in 45s. Worker queue length down.
Elena (OrbitFin): seeing customers reconnect successfully, dashboards back to normal. We'll advise mobile teams to update SDK but that's longer-term.
Mira: good. We'll keep routing + circuit-breaker for 2 hours while patch lands. Raj, ETA on auth patch?
Raj: hotfix build completed, deploying to canary then full at 16:22 UTC. Patch sets `Retry-After: 15` for throttles and fixes header serialization bug.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: auth-service@v3.4.7-hotfix deployed to us-east-2 canary at 2026-03-15T16:20:10Z.
Raj: canary looks good, rolling to cluster. Full roll at 16:24:05Z.
Priya: after patch fully rolled, reconnects normalized to <1% and 429s reduced to baseline.
Mira: documenting action items: (1) QA regression to ensure Retry-After never set to 0, add unit test for header code path, (2) update runbook for tenant-scoped circuit-breaker steps, (3) advise enterprise customers to adopt jittered exponential backoff and honor Retry-After, (4) consider per-tenant connection quotas that persist across routes to avoid worker exhaustion during retries.
Ken: filing NET/INF ticket to add a guard in route switch to preserve global token limiter metadata. TKT-ORBIT-117.
Elena (OrbitFin): thank you. We'll push an advisory to our clients recommending the temporary SDK patch and note that Redwood applied server-side mitigations.
Mira: handing off RCA/postmortem ownership to Raj. I'm unpaging. Raj, you're owner for the postmortem and customer RCA.
Raj: acknowledged, will compile timeline and root cause. Saving logs/traces to s3://redwood-incidents/1965432101/ and adding pack of headers sample to the ticket.
Mira: closing slack incident thread for now. Ops, keep incident ticket open until postmortem published.
